relevance_note: Single case report of a person with a diagnosis of arterial tortuosity syndrome made on imaging: 'a diagnosis of coarctation of the aorta with arterial tortuosity syndrome was made'; no genetic testing or SLC2A10 variant is reported.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; output assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen values. One in-scope person (the single unnamed patient, label 'patient'), in scope by diagnosis of ATS, which was made from CT angiography only; the paper reports no genetic testing and no SLC2A10 variant, so the variants table is empty. Age 16 recorded as age at last evaluation (age at presentation); no age at diagnosis stated separately. Contradiction: the CT abdominal angiogram 'was performed from the top of the aortic arch to the level of the bifurcation' and reports 'The aorta was normal in caliber from the origin to the bifurcation', while the thoracic CT reports about 50% narrowing of the distal aortic arch and severe narrowing of the thoracic aorta; both phenotypic rows are emitted and the checklist item 'stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches' is set to not reported. Possible tension (not treated as a contradiction): 'no significant atherosclerotic changes' vs 'extensive arterial wall calcifications'. Renal artery stenosis was ruled out, which does not exclude the broader checklist item. 'No clear dysmorphic features' was not used to exclude down-slanting palpebral fissures (broad, hedged statement). The Discussion's general ATS description (pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary artery stenosis, lax skin) is about the disease, not this patient. Normal-finding rows (D-27): 'normal first and second heart sounds' recorded as 'abnormal heart sounds' excluded; 'normal in caliber' as 'abnormal aortic caliber' excluded. First author surname split from the header 'Asafu Adjaye Frimpong George' is uncertain.
